3. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are inter alia that the petitioner as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No. 76 of 1996, Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 1996 and Miscellaneous Case No. 78 of 1996 against the pre-emptee-opposite party Nos. 1-9 before the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act (NAT Act). Having received the summons of all the aforesaid three miscellaneous cases, the pre-emptee-opposite parties entered appearance in all the aforesaid three miscellaneous (pre-emption) cases and filed written objections denying the allegations set out therein. Thereafter, all the aforesaid miscellaneous cases were fixed for simultaneously hearing. Eventually, the pre-emptor obtained ex-parte decree in those miscellaneous (pre-emption) cases on 1-10-1995. Thereafter, the pre-emptee-opposite parties filed Miscellaneous Case No. 76 of 1996, Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 1996 and Miscellaneous Case No. 78 of 1996 under Order IX, rule 13 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in short 'the CPC' for setting aside the ex-parte judgment and orders. On 19-1-2005, those were fixed for ex-parte hearing. On that date, all the aforesaid miscellaneous cases were dismissed for default. 

 "On consideration of ratio decidendi of the cited decision, we do not find any reason to take a different view and disturb the long settled decisions followed by the High Court Division and its predecessor High Court on the question for the last thirty years. Apart from the question of disturbing the stare decisis the decisions are based on good reasons. The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act does not provide for any appeal from such an order. The Civil Procedure Code provides appeal from an order rejecting application to set-aside a decree passed ex-parte made in a suit. The application of this rule pre-supposes existence to two conditions which are absent in an order so passed in a proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The first is that the order of refusal is to set-aside an ex-parte decree and the second, that the order is passed in a proceeding which is a suit. None of the conditions being present, the view so long held does not call for any revision." 

 21. For the reasons stated above, all the Rules of Civil Revision No. 1109 of 2011, Civil Revision No. 1110 of 2011 and Civil Revision No. 1111 of 2011 are made absolute; however, without passing any order as to costs. The earlier orders of stay by this Court thus stand vacated and recalled.
